subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context event-loop stalls despite possible prompt-order and session-timing changes?
rationale: The exact-head patch and proof support the performance mechanism, but bootstrap context and hook ordering are compatibility-sensitive session surfaces where automated review cannot choose the acceptable upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Refresh
options.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, require the relevant checks, and merge the focused fix.

options.title: Require Full Embedded-Run Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but request one current-head embedded-run or connected-channel transcript showing channel responsiveness during bootstrap before accepting the risk.

options.title: Pause Or Narrow The Patch
options.body: Hold the PR or split out lower-risk async reads if maintainers do not want a custom glob implementation and hook interleaving on the bootstrap path.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Refresh
recommendation.body: Accept the internal scheduling and glob-resolution tradeoff, rebase onto current main, require the relevant checks, and merge the focused fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged-history trail spans all three decision surfaces: internal hooks, bootstrap hooks, and guarded workspace reads.
